phase2_5_adversarialChallenge.counter: The spec never states what happens to lib/rules.mjs (flow), whose RULES table has 43 severity assignments and whose scan is a thin wrapper over dataflow.mjs. F3 step 12 says 'migrate flow' in four words. That is the largest set and the least specified.

Step 13 says 'update the ~80 summary.* assertions across 11 test files' as one line. That is the single largest mechanical risk in the plan and it has no ordering, no per-file breakdown, and no statement of which assertions are expected to change value rather than shape.

F2 changes when a scan stops reading. Adding the guard to hidden, copybook, jcl and inventory means four sets gain early-stop behaviour they never had. On a constrained CI box this could turn currently-complete scans into incomplete ones, changing test outcomes that assert coverageIncomplete is false.
Challenged on whether F5 actually closes the overclaim path. It does: bySet widening plus setsIncomplete keying is sufficient, and the flag already fires. No grounded reduction.

An earlier framing of H-04 as a silent-wrong-answer was wrong and is corrected here: rules-cics.mjs sets coverageIncomplete from run.skipped.length, and scan.mjs ORs it. Only the diagnostic detail is lost, not the flag.
